analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches, and base/head source. The new model-requant-upload.yml introduces a credentialed model-publication path relevant to A-004, T-012, T-027 and T-007. Visible controls include master-ref checks (105–113, 148–156), secret-free input validation, pinned checkout and hash-required binary dependencies, prod-environment placement (144), bounded job timeouts, quoted environment-based input handling, suppressed credential-probe output (207–208), and upload gating on the selected key set's successful check (268–280). Build and verification precede upload (244–282); no registration or promotion command is visible. No concrete workflow-level security regression is established.

ci-master.yml:175–177 adds offline test discovery without increasing token permissions or changing cache policy. The changelog and docs/developer/test.md patch describe these controls and explicitly avoid claiming native quality or capacity qualification. No supplied change alters prompt encryption, serving authorization, attestation, billing, local privileged helpers, or T-041 cache controls.

Material integration questions remain: examine scripts/models/upload-model-revision.py for URL/path/manifest validation, safe workflow-output emission, byte verification, immutable reservation and overwrite prevention; examine requant.py for download redirects, range parsing, bounded resource use and handling of untrusted model metadata before credentials later enter the same job. The requirements and test implementations are not supplied here, so their guarantees cannot be confirmed. Prod reviewer/bypass policy and actual secret placement are external configuration contracts asserted in comments, not enforced by this YAML alone. Integration should assess whether the new publication boundary needs additional threat-model coverage, without treating the documented pre-existing repository-secret exposure as a regression.
